events.title: Galileo Galilei is born in Pisa
events.description: The future astronomer, physicist and mathematician was born in Pisa, in what is now Italy. He grew up to challenge long-held ideas about the heavens and the laws of motion.
events.significance: Galileo's telescope observations and experiments helped lay the groundwork for modern science. He is often called the father of observational astronomy.

events.title: Women win the right to argue before the U.S. Supreme Court
events.description: President Rutherford B. Hayes signed a bill allowing women attorneys to practice before the nation's highest court.
events.significance: The law opened a door that had been closed to women lawyers. It was an important step toward gender equality in the American legal profession.

events.title: USS Maine explodes in Havana Harbor
events.description: The American battleship USS Maine blew up and sank in the harbor at Havana, Cuba. More than 260 crew members were killed.
events.significance: The sinking inflamed public opinion in the United States. It became a major catalyst for the Spanish-American War later that year.

events.title: Assassination attempt on President-elect Franklin D. Roosevelt
events.description: In Miami, Giuseppe Zangara fired at President-elect Roosevelt but hit Chicago Mayor Anton Cermak instead. Cermak died of his wounds on March 6.
events.significance: Roosevelt was unharmed and took office weeks later to lead the country through the Great Depression. The attack led to greater attention to the security of presidents-elect.

events.title: Singapore falls to Japanese forces
events.description: British General Arthur Percival surrendered Singapore to Japan after a rapid assault. About 80,000 Indian, British and Australian troops became prisoners.
events.significance: It was one of the worst defeats in British military history. It shattered the image of British power in Asia during World War II.
